title.narrative: Sustaining Access to and Quality of Education During Economic Difficulties Project

description.narrative: Mongolia is facing severe economic difficulties. Significant cuts in the education budget for 2017 and beyond greatly constrain the government''s capacity to mitigate further deterioration of education services. This will result in lost opportunities for pre-primary, primary, and secondary education, especially for children who come from disadvantaged backgrounds. Support from the Asian Development Bank is urgently needed to minimize the negative effects during this difficult economic period by (i) narrowing the gap in the enrollment capacity of schools and kindergartens in Ulaanbaatar and some aimag (administrative subdivision) centers, (ii) supporting the completion of unfinished curriculum reform and associated assessment system reforms, (iii) ensuring the provision of teaching and learning materials that accompany the new curriculum, (iv) upgrading the skills and knowledge of teachers and managers for the new curriculum and assessments, and (v) strengthening systems for planning and managing education services.

Output: Indicator Indicator: 25% of schools using the updated framework in their school improvement plans and school report cards by 2025 (2017 baseline: 5%) Achievement: 26 Progress/Status: A total of 184 rural schools, accounting for 26% of total public schools (705 in total), were selected to implement the recommendations including the PDCA approach, School Improvement Plan (SIP), and School Recording Card (SRC). Under the project, 4,682 school administrators and manager from 163 rural schools , along with 350 staff from local education departments in 21 aimags, were trained to use the SIP, SRC and and lesson management following observations of 832 lessons. Since March 2024, online training has been conducted for 920 managers from 184 schools with 662 managers having completed the training. 84 trainers (42 from GAE, 42 from 21 local education departments) were trained to conduct training and monitoring. Monitoring was conducted for 163 rural schools by observing 832 lessons and providing recommendations on school-based management related to the process of developing SIP and SRC for 4,287 persons (458 school managers, 349 head teachers of professional development groups, and 3,380 teachers).
The project aimed to receive 552 deliverables from 184 target schools, each submitting SIP, SCR, and SMD documents. As of the reporting period, 80% (447) of these documents were received.
A workshop summarizing the results and sharing experiences on SBM was conducted for 184 school principals and 21 specialists from local education departments in Ulaanbaatar over two days. Schools and local education departments prepared 92 videos and 109 presentations, which were shared through GAE and the project website.
In total, 8 training were conducted for 4,038 (duplicated) school managers on SBM, focusing on school improvements plan (SIP)s and school report cards (SRC)s. The MOE has been evaluating school performances since 2022. As of 2024, 80% of 184 schools have improved their performances by 2.5%, while student achievement has increased by 11.5% compared to 2022. The guidance and recommendations are being prepared for 184 schools to develop SRCs for 2024-2025 and SIPs for 2025-2026, in alignment with the new curriculum.
Data Source: PIU's annual progress monitoring reports; survey of workshop participants

Output: Indicator Indicator: 60% of pre-primary, primary, and secondary education teachers (of whom more than 85% are female) regularly participating in CPD programs through online platforms by 2026 (2017 baseline: 30%) Achievement: 19 Progress/Status: An IT consulting firm (CS-01) developed an online platform, bagsh.edu.mn, for the GAE. The platform was piloted twice: training was conducted for 150 physics and geography teachers in Q4 2023, and for 1,500 physics and geography teachers in Q1 2024. After improving the system based on pilot results, the GAE used the platform to conduct online training for 3,305 teachers (73% of whom were female, totaling 2,412) in their 1st, 5th, and 10th years through the platform in Q3-4 2024. To upgrade the platform, an additional activity was added to the project's plan. Approvals were obtained from MOF and ADB for the activity, and the procurement process commenced with the establishment of the selection committee in November 2024.. In Q2 2025, 7,085 participants joined, 3,813 primary and 2,068 pre-primary teachers with 5, 10,15 and 20 years of experience received certificates upon successful completion CPD programs through bagsh.edu.mn platform starting from mid-March 2025 until May 2025. Since February 17, professional development training for school training managers responsible for “Teacher Development” has been delivered online via Bagsh.edu.mn, concluding on April 19 with 154 participants. The school leadership module, delivered via Bagsh.edu.mn, engaged 700 school principals, who were awarded digital certificates upon completion. The platform is being used for CPD programs of pre-primary, primary and secondary teachers with 5, 10, and 15 years of experience from 24 March 2025 until 15 May 2025. By May 2024, 17,973 (15,906 or 88.5% were female,47.6% of all primary and secondary teachers) teachers and 1,359 (1,302 or 95.8% were female, 13% of all pre-primary teachers) teachers attended this training. In total, 19,726 (88,5% were women) teachers who have completed 5, 10, or 15 years of service, participated in the core professional development training. This accounts for 41.3% of total 47,715 of all secondary and pre-primary teachers. In 2025, bagsh.edu.mn online platform was expanded with two more modules including “Teacher Development Group and Center” and “Finance” modules in under the package no. CS-05. Between 17 November and 30 December 2025, specialized training was conducted for 28,303 teachers from public secondary schools, of whom 26,270 teachers successfully completed the training and received certificates and for 8,254 teachers from public kindergartens, of whom 7,752 teachers successfully completed the training and received certificates. As of Q4 of 2025, a total of 35,637 (of whom 25,372 or 71.1% female) or 95% of all secondary education teachers, and 8,254 (of whom 7,205 or 87% female) or 78% of all preschool teachers, participated in core professional development and specialized online training. It was identified that sex-disaggregated data for approximately 3,000 teachers was missing for training conducted in 2025, and corrective work is currently being carried out in collaboration with Starsoft LLC and EITC to complete the data.
Data Source: PIU's annual progress monitoring reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: 70% of school managers trained and report improved knowledge in the use of the revised performance-based framework for teachers (of whom 55% are female) to mentor staff and identify CPD needs by 2025 (2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 70 Progress/Status: The EA's appointed working group has developed a training program for school managers responsible for assessment and evaluation. Based on this program, training sessions were conducted for 799 participants, including school managers and local education department staff, to strengthen their understanding of student assessment, teacher appraisal, and school evaluation. Output: Unfinished curriculum reform and associated assessment system reforms completed Indicator: 30% of secondary science teachers (of whom more than 80% are female) trained in science laboratory skills and management by 2025 (2017 baseline: not trained) (OP1.1, OP 2.2) Achievement: 31.3 Progress/Status: Sixty video lessons have been created for science teacher training, covering various subjects (chemistry-11, physics-14, biology-12, geography-10, primary science-7, mathematics-10). A total of 1,097 teachers (representing 31.3% of all science teachers, 85% of whom are women) enhanced their knowledge and skills. Handbook and video contents for 30 experiments for 6-9 grades were developed and submitted to MOE and GAE. The contract for supply of science equipment for secondary schools and a model science laboratory at GAE was awarded in Oct 2025. It is expected that the teachers will be trained in science laboratory skills and management at model laboratory in 2026. Data Source: PIU's annual progress monitoring reports

Output: Systems for planning and managing education services strengthened Indicator: Plan to introduce cluster systems for schools and kindergartens developed and pilot tested by 2023 (2017 baseline: not pilot tested) Achievement: n Progress/Status: The cluster system plan was finalized under package no. CS-04. The MOE assigned a working group to oversee it. Based on the analysis, the consulting firm suggested that the cluster system is more suitable for schools in aimag centers and Ulaanbaatar city, rather than for schools in soums and kindergartens. For piloting the plan, it may not be feasible to test within the project implementation period due to required changes in laws, which may take longer than the project implementation period, as concluded by the working group established under the MOE. On 11 May 2023, the group concluded that piloting the plan was not feasible within the project period due to required legal changes beyond the project's control, which are time-consuming. Thus, the performance indicator is underachieved.
Data Source: MOE's annual report and PIU's annual progress monitoring reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y Actual value: n

Output: Systems for planning and managing education services strengthened Indicator: Real-time information system to identify school and kindergarten construction, expansion, and rehabilitation needs developed with gender-sensitive and inclusive design parameters by 2025 (2017 baseline: not developed) Achievement: n Progress/Status: The real-time information system was developed by a consulting firm under package CS-04 and transferred to EA in 2023. The consulting firm conducted the following activities: - Evaluated and ranked the current situation of schools and kindergartens based on multiple criteria; - Developed a mathematical model to generate the optimal scenario for catchment area and investment planning for the rehabilitation, expansion, and construction of schools; - Prepared a three-year investment plan for the education sector; - Identified catchment areas for kindergarten and school enrollment in Ulaanbaatar for the 2023-2024 academic year through the system, with UMED updating the enrollment catchment areas based on this result. To enhance the usage and effectiveness of the system, the MOE plans to upgrade and integrate it with other asset management and investment systems under package no. CS-06 in 2024-2025. The MOE has requested approval from MOF to fund this activity using the project proceeds. However, the MOF issued a directive on April 22, 2025, not to fund the activity. As a result, it has been excluded from the 2025 plan. Data Source: MOE's information system operating at the beginning of 2020 Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: n

Output: Teachers' and managers' knowledge and skills upgraded for the updated curriculum and assessments Indicator: CPD programs developed for school and kindergarten managers, and Ulaanbaatar and aimag (administrative subdivision) education department staff using online platforms by 2026 (2017 baseline: not developed) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Online modules and training CPD programs on early childhood development assessment were developed. The CPD programs for school leaders and teachers, focusing on child-centered, inclusive approaches and student assessment, were completed. A math and science lesson plan was prepared, piloted, and recorded for CPD programs. Training for 93 trainers (of which 88% or 82 were female) was conducted in Sep-Oct 2024. Training programs for school managers and local Education Department staff were developed and approved by GAE. An online training module is being developed by converting CPD programs for school managers and local ED staff. Trained 90 trainers (21 from GAE, 27 from 9 districts, 42 from 21 aimags). Provided 3-day face-to-face training to 886 participants (695 school principals, 191 local education staff) from 21 aimags and 9 districts. Participants enhanced their knowledge and skills in child-centered, inclusive, and active learning approaches. Subsequently, 10 aimag education departments trained 386 managers and 295 teachers using their teacher development budgets. The developed CPD program for school administrators was uploaded as an online training module on the bagsh.edu.mn platform. The online training was conducted in 9-28 May 2025, engaging 470 school principals (of whom 291, or 62%, were women) and 127 kindergarten managers (of whom 119, or 93.7%, were women), who were all awarded certificates upon completion. Data Source: PIU's annual progress monitoring reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: n Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: n Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

These CPD programs were uploaded at basgh.edu.mn platform in Q2 2025.
